title: Knowledge Doc
content: PROJECT: Plexus (formerly called AURA) is a 24-hour hackathon project for hackCBS 9.0 by Mahi Garg and Bhumika. Pitch: a team of specialist AI agents that share one memory, with a guard layer (injection check, confidence gate, approval, undo) and an audit trail. Positioning: a "System of Action", not a chatbot; an autonomous chief of staff / AI back-office. Core problem: the "administrative routing problem" where people act as human data-transporters between tools. Stance: the problem exists at every company size and compounds with scale; always name a specific user role first (sales engineer answering security questionnaires, IT admin handling access requests, finance person chasing receipts), then show it scales. Target prize: the Meko-powered AI Agent prize (YugabyteDB is title sponsor). Demo story uses the same names everywhere: Nimbus Labs (a 40-person B2B startup) lands a deal with Meridian Bank.

title: Knowledge Doc
content: PLEXUS FEATURES. Original 9 were cut to 6, framed as three jobs: Win the deal (RFP), Run the work (ActionSwarm, IT access, search), Control the spend (expenses, Zombie SaaS). F1 RFP and Security Questionnaire Engine (the wedge, real build): upload Excel/CSV, knowledge base of SOC2 docs/policies, answer per question with citation, confidence gate (auto-fill above threshold, red flag below with closest source), human review UI, learning loop (corrected answers saved and reused on next questionnaire), export .xlsx plus accuracy report. F2 ActionSwarm (real): meeting transcript to schema-forced JSON of action items, assignees, due dates; tasks on own dashboard board (real Jira optional); Slack summary post; email draft; live activity feed; injection guard that treats planted instructions as data. F3 OmniContext + Catch-Me-Up (Cmd+K, real over ~10 seeded docs): hybrid search with cited answers, permission-aware retrieval (intern vs founder salary-sheet demo; needs confirmation that Meko datapack sharing supports this), Catch-Me-Up is a time-window mode ("last 4 days") giving an executive briefing. F4 ZeroTouch Expenses (thin): 3-5 prepared receipts via Gemini vision, extract merchant/items/GST/total, policy check, one violation, card-feed matching. F5 Zero-Friction IT Provisioning (real logic): natural-language request ("I need Figma"), risk classification, role check, low-risk auto-grant, high-risk (AWS prod) manager Approve/Reject (dashboard button, Slack button if time), audit log and undo. F6 Zombie SaaS Eradicator (mocked on purpose): seeded billing and SSO login tables, one SQL join for tools paid for with zero logins in 30+ days, waste dashboard in rupees. CUT (roadmap slide only): Dynamic Pitch-Deck Compiler, Procurement and Contract Routing. Priority: RFP engine plus trust layer must never be cut; cut order if behind: Zombie SaaS, Expenses, Slack buttons, Catch-Me-Up. On slides use feature names, not numbers.

title: Knowledge Doc
content: PLEXUS TECHNICAL FINDINGS (Oct 30 2026). GEMINI: rate limits apply per Google PROJECT, not per API key (a second key in the same project gives no extra quota; Bhumika's key must be in her own project). Per-model RPM/TPM/RPD are no longer in public docs; they are shown only on the logged-in page aistudio.google.com/rate-limit (pick the project that holds the key). Free tier: Google may use prompts to improve its products and humans may review them, so only fake seed data goes in, and the pitch must not claim zero data retention. TEST RESULTS from gemini-test.js (a single-file Node script, 10 RFP questions per call, JSON schema reply, run 5 times): model gemini-3.6-flash: 200 OK on 3 of 5 runs, each correct (valid JSON, 8/8 answerable questions correct, the 2 unanswerable ones flagged), about 7 seconds per call, 1,472 to 1,885 tokens per call; the other 2 runs failed with HTTP 503 "high demand" (transient server load, not quota), so retry with backoff is mandatory. Model gemini-pro-latest: all 5 calls HTTP 429 quota exceeded within about half a second, which suggests no free-tier quota, so do not use it. DECISION: use gemini-3.6-flash for both FAST and SMART slots (extraction, receipts via vision, briefings); add a second flash/lite model as GEMINI_MODEL_FALLBACK after 3 failed tries; retry on 503 and 429 (about 2s, 4s, 8s); run batches 2 at a time; Demo Mode replays recorded JSON. At ~7 s per 10-question call, 50 questions is about 35 s sequentially (untested if parallel). MEKO: a TypeScript or script client authenticates with an API key only (no OAuth): generate it in Meko portal Settings > API Keys > Generate (key starts mko_tkn_, shown only once, expires after 1 year, scoped to the account not one datapack). Send two headers on every request to https://mcp.mekodata.ai/mcp: `Authorization: Bearer mko_tkn_...` and `User-Agent: meko-mcp-installer/1.0`. Do not use X-Api-Key or MEKO_API_KEY as header names; do not configure OAuth and the key together. Meko tool quirks seen from Claude: every tool call needs a conversation_id (create with conversation_create, which takes an agent_id and optional datapack_id). Meko-hosted AMP databases need the Pro tier, so app data lives in local SQLite. Mahi's account: Mahi Garg, mahigarg0403@gmail.com. Datapacks: plexus-hackcbs-9 (id e2e101d5-5f68-4672-8343-0c809adb98f2, the project datapack) and meko_default_datapack (id a2f7c063-5bf2-46ca-83c4-1f5911f2197b, empty). Plexus conversation id for tool calls: ef6175c9d1cd428c87596966bc72bd49 (agent_id claude_ai:plexus_hackcbs). Knowledge search works (verified by querying the cut order). Bhumika's access to the datapack is still unresolved: no sharing tool was found from Claude, so check the Meko dashboard or Discord.
